title: PAH-OMC-020 owner-inventory replay drift after R-527
question: After the R-527 source-multiplicity checkpoint added new proof files, do the earlier N2a owner-intake and R-526 stable-inventory checks still replay byte-for-byte?
finding: No. The N2a contract check aborts at its pinned N2b parent: expected SHA-256 034f5fc35a88a4431ee1594c8a25e0d7bcf6c75b055ec2b21bbf30daf636dc7f but the current N2b result is b87a2d8d7b0009c9f5bd30695823cb442376939ff18c1d48f1d890ae430fe8c7. The R-526 dynamic inventory check also reports replay mismatch because its current-file and reachable-history counts changed after the R-527 files were added. The scoped R-527 integrated verifier and the N2b self-check remain independent and passing.
decision_reason: This is a provenance/replay-stability defect in older dynamic audits, not a mathematical counterexample and not evidence that the PAH temporal target fails. Historical hash-pinned artifacts are left untouched; the defect is recorded so a successor frozen snapshot can be supplied rather than silently rewriting old evidence or reporting a stale PASS.
boundary: PAH-001, PAH-OMC-020 preregistration, R-510/R-511/R-512 target, original labelled rates, Gibbs state, external Markov time and j-before-n order remain unchanged. Only current-worktree replay behavior of the earlier owner-inventory and intake audits is examined.
method: Run the pinned N2a owner-packet contract replay without a packet and retain the exact first failing parent hash comparison.
Run the R-526 stable owner-inventory replay and compare its stored path count and digest with the current dynamic inventory without overwriting the historical output.
Run the N2b scoped self-check and the R-527 integrated verifier to separate the replay defect from the current finite source-multiplicity evidence.
Keep the old R-526 and N2a hashes immutable and define a successor frozen-snapshot requirement instead of editing history.
next_action: Create a versioned fixed-snapshot owner-inventory successor and a matching N2a intake successor that pins the current N2b bytes; rerun the owner checks only against that immutable snapshot, then resume the temporal obligations if a source-authorized packet appears.
revisit_condition: Reopen the replay audit when a clean fixed checkpoint or a versioned source-owner packet is available. Do not rewrite R-526, the v1.0 N2a contract, or the R-527 result to conceal the observed drift.
non_claims: No PAH-OMC-020 semigroup convergence, N2a/N2b/N2c/N4/N2d theorem or negative result is claimed.
No universal impossibility follows from a stale dynamic inventory or parent-hash mismatch.
No PAH-001 functional, rate, state, carrier, regulator, time or limit-order change.
No physical Pre-A, spacetime, QFT, gravity, continuum, mass-gap, Yang-Mills or TOE conclusion.
verification_summary: Current probes: N2a owner-intake --check FAILS at the stale N2b parent hash; R-526 owner-inventory --check FAILS on dynamic replay drift; N2b common-space --check passes 22/22; R-527 integrated verifier passes 33/33 with Lean. This record is an evidence-integrity correction, not a mathematical closure.
